title: Match parser settings to the input contract
description: Choose an input boundary and a parser profile. The result shows why format, validation, recovery, entity handling, and parser limits must be explicit production decisions.

scenarios.label: Internal configuration
scenarios.detail: Small, well-formed XML produced by a controlled build pipeline.
scenarios.contract: Reject malformed XML and return one complete tree without loading external resources.

bounded-xml.headline: Strict XML parsing matches the configuration contract
bounded-xml.explanation: The profile rejects malformed XML, keeps parser limits enabled, avoids DTD loading, and does not resolve entities.
actions: Keep a byte limit at the file or transport boundary.
Test the expected namespace and root element after parsing.

schema-xml.headline: Schema validation is useful only if a maintained schema is part of the contract
schema-xml.explanation: An XML Schema can enforce structure and types, but it adds a versioned dependency that this simple configuration flow may not need.
actions: Use this profile only when the schema is authoritative and versioned with producers.
Surface schema error-log details without leaking sensitive input.

recover-html.headline: An HTML recovery parser changes the format contract
recover-html.explanation: HTML recovery is designed to repair tag soup. Configuration XML requires XML well-formedness and must fail rather than silently reshape invalid input.
actions: Use XMLParser for XML documents.
Keep recover disabled for configuration correctness.

huge-trusted-xml.headline: Disabling parser protections has no benefit for a bounded configuration
huge-trusted-xml.explanation: The input is small, so huge_tree expands the accepted resource envelope without satisfying a missing requirement.
actions: Retain normal parser limits.
Investigate unexpected depth or text growth as a producer defect.

scenarios.label: Partner XML feed
scenarios.detail: A contractual business feed must match a versioned XML Schema before records are accepted.
scenarios.contract: Reject well-formed documents that violate required fields, types, or element ordering in the agreed XSD.

bounded-xml.headline: Well-formed is not the same as contract-valid
bounded-xml.explanation: Strict XML parsing catches syntax errors, but it does not prove that the feed satisfies the partner schema.
actions: Compile the trusted XSD once and attach it to the validating profile.
Quarantine invalid documents with a bounded error summary.

schema-xml.headline: The validating parser enforces the partner contract while parsing
schema-xml.explanation: The schema checks structure and types, while the parser profile keeps network loading and entity replacement out of the document path.
actions: Version schemas and fixtures with the integration contract.
Test old and new producers during schema rollout.

recover-html.headline: HTML recovery cannot enforce an XML Schema contract
recover-html.explanation: The parser may repair malformed markup into an HTML tree instead of rejecting invalid XML and validating the required XSD.
actions: Parse the feed as XML.
Use XMLSchema validation for the agreed schema language.

huge-trusted-xml.headline: A larger parser envelope does not add schema validation
huge-trusted-xml.explanation: huge_tree relaxes parser limits; it does not prove required fields, types, or ordering.
actions: Keep resource limits independent from validation.
Select the schema profile for this contract.

scenarios.label: Malformed public HTML
scenarios.detail: Authorized page markup may contain broken nesting, omitted elements, and non-XML HTML conventions.
scenarios.contract: Recover a usable HTML tree, then verify selectors against fixtures and reject unexpected page shapes downstream.

bounded-xml.headline: Strict XML parsing rejects common HTML syntax
bounded-xml.explanation: HTML is not simply lenient XML. Real pages may rely on HTML recovery rules and void-element syntax that violate XML well-formedness.
actions: Use HTMLParser for HTML input.
Test the recovered tree rather than assuming browser-identical repair.

schema-xml.headline: XML Schema validation targets the wrong document contract
schema-xml.explanation: A page extraction pipeline needs a recovered HTML tree and application-level selector checks, not an unrelated XSD.
actions: Choose an HTML parser profile.
Validate extracted records after parsing.

recover-html.headline: The HTML parser matches the recovery requirement
recover-html.explanation: The parser can build a tree from malformed HTML. Recovery still requires fixtures because repaired structure can differ from source text and browser DOM behavior.
actions: Bound response bytes before parsing.
Assert selector cardinality and required fields on representative fixtures.

huge-trusted-xml.headline: A huge XML parser is still the wrong format parser
huge-trusted-xml.explanation: Relaxing XML parser limits does not provide HTML recovery semantics and unnecessarily widens the resource envelope.
actions: Use HTMLParser with normal limits.
Separate acquisition limits from parsing.

scenarios.label: Untrusted XML upload
scenarios.detail: A user-supplied XML document must be parsed without external resource access or expanded parser limits.
scenarios.contract: Keep the parse bounded, reject malformed input, and treat parser settings as one layer inside byte, time, and worker-isolation controls.

bounded-xml.headline: The bounded profile is the appropriate starting boundary
bounded-xml.explanation: It keeps normal parser restrictions, does not load a DTD, blocks network lookup, and leaves entity references unresolved.
actions: Enforce byte and time limits before and around parsing.
Isolate workers and validate the resulting application data.

schema-xml.headline: Validation can narrow accepted structure but does not replace resource controls
schema-xml.explanation: A trusted, local schema may help when uploads have a formal contract. The validating profile still needs transport limits and isolated execution.
actions: Load only a locally controlled schema.
Keep entity and network settings explicit.

recover-html.headline: Recovery hides XML correctness failures
recover-html.explanation: The upload contract is XML. It should reject malformed input rather than reinterpret it as recoverable HTML.
actions: Use strict XML parsing.
Return a bounded syntax error to the caller.

huge-trusted-xml.headline: huge_tree removes protections at the least trusted boundary
huge-trusted-xml.explanation: The official parser option exists for very deep trees and long text by disabling parser security restrictions. That is the opposite of this upload contract.
actions: Keep huge_tree disabled.
Reject documents that exceed the bounded parser and application envelope.

scenarios.label: Oversized trusted export
scenarios.detail: A controlled producer emits legitimate XML that exceeds normal depth or text limits after independent size review.
scenarios.contract: Accept the documented oversized shape only after proving the producer, byte envelope, worker isolation, and downstream algorithm are bounded.

bounded-xml.headline: Keep normal limits unless a representative fixture proves they block valid input
bounded-xml.explanation: The bounded profile is safer and should remain the default. A real parser-limit failure is evidence for a narrowly reviewed exception, not a reason to preemptively expand every worker.
actions: Capture the exact parser error and representative fixture.
Prefer changing the producer or using a streaming shape when possible.

schema-xml.headline: Schema correctness and parser resource limits are independent
schema-xml.explanation: A valid document may still exceed normal parser protections. Schema validation alone does not authorize a larger resource envelope.
actions: Validate structure if the feed contract requires it.
Review parser limits separately.

recover-html.headline: HTML recovery cannot solve a legitimate XML size limit
recover-html.explanation: Switching formats would change names, validation, and failure behavior instead of addressing the bounded exception.
actions: Keep XML semantics.
Measure whether streaming avoids the need for a full retained tree.

huge-trusted-xml.headline: Use huge_tree only as a documented, isolated exception
huge-trusted-xml.explanation: The option allows very deep trees and long text by disabling parser restrictions. It can be appropriate for proven legitimate input only when external limits still bound the job.
actions: Restrict the profile to this controlled producer and measured worker class.
Retain byte, time, concurrency, and output limits outside the parser.

profiles.label: Bounded strict XML
profiles.detail: Reject malformed XML, keep normal parser limits, and avoid DTD or entity expansion.
safeguards: DTD loading and entity replacement are disabled.
Normal depth and text protections remain enabled.

profiles.label: Schema-validating XML
profiles.detail: Validate against a compiled, locally controlled XML Schema while parsing.
safeguards: The schema is trusted application configuration, not document-supplied code.
Malformed or schema-invalid documents fail the parse.
Schema versions and producer compatibility still need release management.

profiles.label: Recover external HTML
profiles.detail: Use HTML parsing semantics for authorized page markup and verify the repaired tree with fixtures.
safeguards: The input is treated as HTML, not XML.
Application selectors validate the recovered tree shape.

profiles.label: Reviewed huge XML
profiles.detail: Relax depth and text restrictions only for a controlled, independently bounded producer.
safeguards: Transport bytes, worker time, concurrency, and output remain externally bounded.
The profile is not available to untrusted inputs.
